items.stem: An AI tool provides a perfectly formatted citation for a claim. What must the researcher do before using it?

options.text: Verify the reference actually exists and supports the claim
options.rationale: Correct: AI commonly fabricates plausible-looking citations.

options.text: Use it because the formatting is correct
options.rationale: Formatting does not prove the source exists.

options.text: Cite it without reading the source
options.rationale: Citing unverified, unread sources breaches integrity.

items.explanation: Correct: AI commonly fabricates plausible-looking citations.

items.stem: Which TWO practices uphold research integrity when using AI? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Disclose how AI was used, per journal and institutional policy
options.rationale: Correct: transparency about AI use is a core integrity norm.

options.text: Keep a human author accountable for all content
options.rationale: Correct: accountability cannot be delegated to a tool.

options.text: List the AI tool as a co-author
options.rationale: AI tools generally cannot meet authorship criteria.

options.text: Use AI to draft results without running the study

items.explanation: Correct: transparency about AI use is a core integrity norm.

items.stem: Why is relying only on an AI summary of a key paper risky in a literature review?

options.text: The summary may omit or distort findings the review depends on
options.rationale: Correct: AI summaries can be incomplete or inaccurate.

options.text: Summaries are always complete and accurate
options.rationale: AI summaries can miss or misstate key points.

options.text: Reading the paper is never necessary
options.rationale: Verifying against the source is essential.
